svg.title: Figure 40.8 — Tropilaelaps Life Cycle and Brood Dependence
svg.desc: Life cycle of Tropilaelaps mercedesae showing entry into a partially capped brood cell, reproduction during prepupal/pupal stages, adult emergence and brief dispersal before re-entering brood.
svg.text: Figure 40.8 — Tropilaelaps Life Cycle and Brood Dependence
Tropilaelaps spends nearly its entire reproductive cycle in sealed brood and has only a brief adult-bee dispersal phase.
Mated female enters a late-larval / partially capped brood cell.
Egg laying begins as the host reaches prepupal development.
Larval → protonymph → deutonymph → adult mite stages develop in the cell.
Adult mites emerge as the host bee emerges.
Adults typically survive briefly on adult bees/comb before seeking brood.
Brood availability is essential for continued reproduction.

text.tspan: Recent review evidence places the adult-bee dispersal period at roughly 1–2 days in typical conditions. Do not depict Tropilaelaps as
completely incapable of short survival or dispersal outside brood.
